paper_id: Towards Cross-Project Defect Prediction with Imbalanced Feature Sets
title: Towards Cross-Project Defect Prediction with Imbalanced Feature Sets
motivation: Public defect datasets have different metric sets, making cross-project prediction infeasible due to the identical-feature assumption in regular CPDP, causing redundant data collection.
problem_framing: Define CPDP-IFS where source and target projects have different metric sets, requiring a mapping to a common latent space.
key_insight: Instances with different feature vectors may have similar statistical distributions of normalized metric values, making distribution characteristics a potential bridge.
method_signature: Distribution characteristic-based instance mapping: preprocess → project onto latent space of indicators → apply regular CPDP.
evaluation_criteria: f-measure with Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Cliff's Delta for statistical significance and effect size.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Only used logistic regression; all projects are Java-based; feature selection on 16 indicators not explored.
evidence_for_taste: distribution characteristics seems to be proper components of the latent space
the great correlation coefficients indicate a significantly linear correlation
at least the introduction of CPDP-IFS does not have a negative effect
CPDP-IFS can be a sound complement to the regular CPDP
thinking_moves: 把特征集合不同的问题转化为分布特征空间的映射问题
用统计分布特性(均值/方差/中位数)替代原始特征向量作为跨项目桥接
先验证方法优于简单交集法,再证与常规CPDP可比,最后构建混合模型
通过DPR指标关联分析找到CPDP-IFS何时有效的工作边界
